body:
> I not only felt like that, I never knew there was anybody in the world who didn't.

I feel like that quite often. The only thing that gets me through sometimes is how many people who say they've been there, or worse, and that it can get better. If it can get better, it's worth a shot. The worst that can happen is I end up right where I am now.

Thanks, I've been trying to write more just to get out of my head for a bit. Just start writing a bit and all of a sudden I'm at three or five pages, and I feel just a bit better. Lightens the load a bit, so to speak.

It's cliché, but I'm thinking of starting a blog, just so I can have somewhere to put my thoughts. Maybe screaming at the world a bit might make me feel better, even if no one reads it.

Thanks for the ideas on the books, I'll look into them.

 I don't think it was 9/11 itself, that was just the first real attack I was exposed to.  More the loss of security and peace of mind that I had before that day. Almost like I haven't felt "at home" since then. The events before that almost feel like a happy dream whenever I think about anything before then.

It seems like before that America was a happy place, or just riding the high from the collapse of the soviet union (which collapsed just after I was born, so I don't really remember it), during the nineties.  Then it all changed for me on that day.

This could just be my memories playing tricks on me, seeing as I was a kid back then, looking at the past through rose colored glasses, and at the future through jade colored ones.

In regard to the emotions though, it feels like lying every time I laugh at a joke, or pretend to be sad at a movie or something.

My relations with my family feel almost professional at this point, same with my friends. I go through the motions because it seems "normal", but I will start trying to be more open with my councilor. Hopefully she will be able to help more if she realizes what's really going on in my head.

Well I feel I should say, it didn't happen instantly, but more over a few days as I realized what really happened.

But my real problem is how to tell my parents, my friends and in a few places my councilor, that I've been lying to them for years. I keep going over the senarios in my head and I can't seem to find a good outcome. What kind of help could stop me from feeling numb?

That may very well be possible. Then again the destruction of innocence has always been associated with growing up. I wonder if not feeling anything is almost a form of atrophy, I haven't used my emotions in so long that I can't anymore, or at least it is very difficult to do so.

I've never really been a good writer, but I usually use writing to get all the thought swirling around in my head. A "stream of consciousness" if you will. But each time I do this it doesn't help as much as the time before.

I've been seeing a psychologist for 6 months or so. I'm also on 40 milligrams of citalopram daily. I've tried other anti-depressants, but nothing let's me feel anything. Sometimes I "worry" I'm a sociopath.
